Subject: Re: SLA options & credits — BrightGrid procurement

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here is starting to map the reliability requirements for our new generative workflow platform and we want to understand how Redwood packages SLA and premium support. A few specific asks:

- What uptime tiers do you offer (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) and how do credits scale?
- Typical time-to-recover (TTR) windows per tier and the escalation coverage (on-call hours / regional handoff).
- Is there a separate rapid-response retainer or is that folded into premium plans?
- Any standard volume-commit discounts for 12/24 month contracts, and how that interacts with credits/retainers.

I attached our short RFI for context. Can we get a concise proposal (one-pager) and a pricing spreadsheet? Ideally by Friday so procurement can slot it into vendor evaluation.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Procurement — BrightGrid

Sanjay —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a pricing model and a short one-pager that maps out three recommended configurations. High level here:

- Standard: 99.9% uptime, business-hours escalation, credits starting at 10% for a single downtime incident over the month.
- Enhanced: 99.95% uptime, 24x7 L1 triage with regional failover, credits scale to 20%.
- Mission-critical: 99.99% formal SLA, dedicated on-call retainer + prioritized capacity, credits up to 40% with faster TTR SLAs.

Volume-commit: we typically offer a sliding discount (5–15%) based on committed spend and term; 12-month commitments usually get 5–7% off list, with higher accreditation for larger multi-year deals. Rapid-response can be an optional retainer (flat monthly) or included in higher tiers.

I put the details in the spreadsheet: redwood_sla_pricing_model_v3.xlsx (attached). If acceptable, I can convert to a formal SOW and DocuSign link. Want to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,

Jonas / Grace —

Sanjay (BrightGrid procurement) sent the RFI and asked for a concise one-pager + pricing by Friday. BrightGrid is evaluating 3rd-party inference vendors and is sensitive to both cost and predictable recovery economics. They asked explicitly about: credits scaling, TTR windows, escalation coverage, and commitment discounts.

Questions:
1) For mission-critical 99.99%, what do we recommend for a guaranteed TTR (e.g., 1 hour for SEV1) and what on-call retainer would we attach?
2) For sliding discounts, do we default to our standard 5/10/15% bands by annual committed spend, or make a special 10% for 12-month with a 20% increase in committed capacity?
3) Any redlines from a support/ops perspective on including regional failover guarantees in the SOW?

Quick thoughts welcome — I'll have a call if needed but want to draft a tight offer.

Marissa

Marissa —

High level recommendations (keeps commercial simple, protects ops):

- SKU A (Standard): 99.9% uptime, TTR: P1 within 8 hours business-hours, no 24x7 retainer. Credits: up to 10% monthly.
- SKU B (Enhanced): 99.95% uptime, TTR: P1 within 4 hours, 24x7 L1 triage included; optional rapid-response retainer for <1hr on-call (<$Xk/mo). Credits: up to 20% monthly with decreasing slab for repeated events.
- SKU C (Mission-critical): 99.99% uptime, TTR: P1 within 1 hour, dedicated named escalation contact + retainer (~$25k/mo typical), regional capacity reservation (best-effort cross-region failover). Credits: up to 40% monthly with cap tied to retainer value.

Discounting guidance: keep the published bands (5% @ 12m min commit, 10% @ 24m, 15% @ 36m), but we can front-load a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 5% of first-year invoices) for competitive deals instead of higher recurring discounts. That preserves unit economics.

Ops redlines: do not promise hard multi-region RPO/RTO in SOW; offer 'regional failover best-effort with documented runbook' and include an optional paid tabletop/DR run for integration customers.

Grace, Priyom — any objections?

Jonas

Agree with Jonas. A couple of additions from an SRE/support perspective:

- For Mission-critical, the retainer should explicitly include quarterly runbook validation sessions and one emergency DR drill per year — helps us avoid surprise scope.
- Credits calculation: tie credits to measurable latency/availability telemetry we can validate in Console. Include an explicit dispute window (30 days) and a cap at 3x monthly retainer to protect ops.
- Response escalation: define L1/L2/L3 handoffs and include a named escalation path in the SOW; also offer optional on-prem engineering hours for integration day-1 (billable).

I'll attach a short support annex we can include in the SOW.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
